DONE **Head: `e9e6ee255a095c67a0e90c7471b6f2dd548ddfbe` on `w1/W1-02`; nothing is committed after it and the tree is clean.** DP-6, DP-7 and DP-8 are built as DEC-553 decides them; every acceptance suite, the unit tests and the validator are green. Nothing of DP-1 is built and no case of another suite was rewritten. ## Commits of this run (on top of `f0c352a5`) | Commit | Role | Task | Implements | What | |---|---|---|---|---| | `56df3da6` | independent-test-designer | DAEO-emkd | CAP-58.a | 383 acceptance cases for DEC-553, red first; no `Rewrite-Reason` (nothing rewritten) | | `869f1505` | orchestrator | DAEO-emkd | CAP-58.a | checkpoint CP-0008 after red was checked | | `bfb4824e` | engineer | DAEO-emkd | CAP-58.a | the three points | | `e9e6ee25` | orchestrator | DAEO-emkd | CAP-58.a | checkpoint CP-0009 before the return | I checked each commit's three trailers myself; none is missing and none needed amending. ## What was built - **DP-6:** the one condition that kept a wildcard-only glob from a copy's `

` allowed is removed. `

` and the session's root now go through the same lines, so what the root allows (a single star in Glob or a shell word, a pattern deeper than the file) is allowed from `

` too. - **DP-7:** the helper also redacts a deny path spelled from the home folder, as written and with `HOME` in its place. With `HOME` unset, empty or `/`, only the as-written spelling is redacted. A rule that is the home folder itself blanks nothing. - **DP-8:** a move, a link or a linking copy whose source is a folder strictly between `

` and the file is refused by the read rule for every role. `

` itself and folders above it are not taken in. - **Refusal text:** unchanged, no path. - **Size:** source +34 / −18 in `protected.py` and `hooks.py`; `decide.py` and the hook are untouched. Builder tests +78 / −2. ## Suites, as I ran them at `bfb4824e` Three parallel streams, each well under two hours, none with `-x`. - **W1-02:** 1690 passed. The latency case passed inside the run. - **W1-05:** 99 passed, latency case included. - **W1-46:** 493 passed, live sessions included. - **W1-50:** 666 passed. **W1-47:** 970. **W1-28:** 149. **W1-38:** 87. **W1-32:** 81. - **Every other acceptance suite** (W1-01, W1-03, W1-04, W1-06 to W1-27, W1-29 to W1-31, W1-33 to W1-37, W1-39, W1-40, W1-44, W1-45, W1-48, W1-49): exit 0, no failure. Skips are the same as in run 2: 28 in W1-01, 1 in W1-26. - **Unit tests:** 1710 passed. **Validator:** ALL PASS. - No case needed a re-run alone this time. - **Red check before the engineer:** 235 failed, 148 passed. Every failure was on the decision or the helper's output, none on an import, fixture or crash. - **Merge check:** `git diff w1/integrate HEAD -- tests/acceptance` lists only files under `tests/acceptance/W1-02/`. ## Comparison over random calls against `750d57fb` 840,000 calls (two seeds of 420,000, same generator as run 2 with folder and linking-copy atoms added): - **Refused before and allowed now: 0.** - **Stricter now: 718** (363 and 355). - **Raises: 3 at the head, the same 3 at `750d57fb`.** This run introduces none. All three are a Bash command holding `~` followed by a NUL byte: `os.path.expanduser` raises `ValueError` in `_expand_token` of `decide.py`, which this run did not touch. `decide.py` does not catch it around the read rule; I did not run the hook process on such an input, so whether that ends as a refusal or a crash exit is not confirmed. Returned as a finding below. - A project with neither file: nothing refused. - **Helper**, 20,000 random settings under five `HOME` values: prints more than before 0, redacts more 320, raises 0. ## Diff read line by line **A forbidden read let through:** none found. Both edits in `protected.py` only add ways to return a refusal. The pattern in `hooks.py` matches every rule it matched before and the home spelling in addition. **Ordinary work stopped:** none found among the named daily forms, all still allowed on stand-in files: - `mv`, `ln -s`, `cp -al`, `git mv` of folders that hold neither file; - such a folder as the destination of a move; - wildcard-only globs from `src`, `docs`, a home subfolder, a sibling's `src`; - globs from `template` or home by name or extension; - `ls -la`, `git add -A`, `git status`, commit, pytest, the helper. **New refusals a session will meet:** - Glob or shell `**/*` and `*/*` with `template`, another worktree's root, or the home folder as the start. - Grep with glob `*` there. - `mv`, `ln` or `cp -al` of a holding folder, for every role. **Beyond the cases (engineer's report, stricter):** - `sed` with a backup suffix and a holding folder as an operand is refused. - The helper blanks a home-spelled deny path also as the first characters of a longer name (`~/a` in `~/abc`), as item 14 already records for absolute paths. ## Findings and what was done - **Two builder cases held the old behaviour** (the designer returned this as DP-9): a Glob over everything from `

` as let through, and a home spelling as printing unchanged. Both are the engineer's own unit cases on the ticket's paths and DEC-553 decides the behaviour, so the engineer moved exactly those lines to the refused and redacted side and kept every neighbour. Flagged because the designer framed it as a package; the README's package section still lists it. - **The pre-existing raise on `~…NUL`** is not fixed; it needs a red case first and is outside this run's three points. Residual 31 below. - No reviewer was commissioned, as ordered; the probe is yours. ## Packages None open from this run. DP-1 is still with the owner (below). ## Residuals, renumbered **What a command-line guard cannot see:** 1. A script file that opens either file. 2. A script on the command line that builds the name. 3. An interpreter or shell fed by a pipe or standard input. 4. A name that arrives at run time (substitution, a variable the command sets, `xargs`, `find -exec`); refused for writes, not held for reads. 5. A command that names no path and reads the tree or history (`git diff` with no path, `git show`, `git log -p`, `git grep`, `rg` with no path, an archive of the root). 6. A git object read by its id. 7. A second name or copy made earlier, outside the call. 8. A program that reads the settings file by itself (`claude`, `rulesync`). 9. A tool the guard does not know (an MCP file tool). 10. to 12. The second batch's three items stand as written in the suite README; I did not re-read their text in this run (11 concerns `git -C` and a `cd` into a folder that exists only at run time, per item 18). **From DEC-548 and DEC-553:** 13. Helper: a deny path spelled project-relative, held bare, prints (held as printing; DEC-553). 14. Helper: the tail of a longer path that starts with a deny path; also a longer name that starts with it. 15. A copy reached by a glob or search that starts above `

` (with DP-1); a search from `

` with no glob follows DP-1. 16. A path that ends in a file's project-relative path and names no existing file yet. 17. A copy under another name or relative path. 18. `git -C ` with a relative path; `cd` into a `

` that exists only at run time. 19. A second name by a program the guard does not know (`rsync --link-dest`, `install`, `cp --reflink`, `git mv`, `tar`, `rename`, a bind mount, an editor's backup). 20. In-place options the guard cannot tell from a suffix (`sed -i bak` without a dot; other programs' in-place suffix options). 21. A user-level settings file that is not at `$HOME` of the hook's environment. 22. A wildcard-only word in a command that is no reader, and other spellings of "everything", are not held one by one. 23. A `

` the guard cannot resolve from the command line, or a copy that appears later in the same command. 24. Helper: the home folder spelled `$HOME/…`, `${HOME}/…`, `~user/…` or through a symbolic link inside a hook command. 25. Helper: the resolved spelling when the helper's `HOME` is missing or differs from the hooks' `HOME`. 26. Helper: a deny rule whose path is the home folder itself blanks nothing. 27. A holding folder reached by a glob in the word, or through an earlier symbolic link. 28. A move or link of `

` itself or of a folder above it. No case either way; afterwards the file lies at the same project-relative path under the new name, which the rule covers as a copy. 29. A move or copy with an option the operand reader cannot read (DEC-553). 30. A copy that is itself a symbolic link to a file elsewhere, named through a path that resolves to the link's target (run 2's engineer). 31. A Bash command holding `~` followed by a NUL byte raises in the unchanged `_expand_token`; the same at `750d57fb`. ## DP-1, still with the owner As built: a search with no glob from the project root, or from a copy's `

`, is allowed for every role, so either file's content can come back from one root search. A glob over everything from the root is refused. If the owner refuses the root search: - one more rule in the guard and about 10 new cases here; - 14 cases rewritten by their designers with `Rewrite-Reason`, in four suites: W1-02 `test_role_less_session_can_still_read_with_file_tools`, W1-50 `test_ticket_lead_may_read[Grep]`, W1-47 `test_a_call_that_names_another_path_stays_allowed[…Grep]` (6), W1-05 `test_a_read_only_tool_goes_through_the_hook_and_is_allowed` (6); - every session then needs a path or a glob for a root search; - residual 15's first half (a start above `

`) is answered with it. My recommendation is unchanged: refuse, medium confidence. ## Interface as built - `python3 -m gov.guard.hooks` prints a JSON array of `{event, matcher, command}`. Deny values are redacted, and so are deny paths spelled absolute (`Tool(//…)`) or from the home folder (`Tool(~/…)`, as written and resolved). Exit 1 with fixed text if the file cannot be read. - `gov.guard.protected.read_refusal(tool_name, tool_input, project_root, cwd)` returns the fixed refusal text or `""`. ## Learning metrics - **KPI disputes:** none. - **Acceptance tests rewritten after implementation began:** 0. - **Tests added after implementation:** 0 acceptance; 4 builder tests added and 2 adjusted by the engineer. - **Source lines:** +34 / −18. No estimate was given for this run; the DP-6 part is the "two-line change" run 2's engineer predicted. - **Engineer iterations:** converged. - **False findings:** none. ## Other - **Guard liveness:** the hooks of this worktree run the guard from this worktree's files (run 2's finding, recorded in CP-0008). My own calls ran behind `bfb4824e` from the moment it landed without a wrong refusal. - **Temp folders left:** none. The probes' stand-in folders were removed and the workers' temp folders went with their sessions. - **Scratch:** briefs `td-4.md` and `eng-4.md`, logs, `probe5.py`, `probe5_forms.py` and `log/verify3/` are under `.gov-runtime/scratch/lead/`. - **Connectors:** Gmail and Google Calendar are not authorised in this session; nothing here needed them.
